question: What was the average real-time price at ERCOT's hub average in 2023 (ERCOT's local year)?
first_answer: The average real-time price at the ERCOT hub average (HB_HUBAVG) in 2023 was 48.36 USD/MWh (ercot_all_hub_prices_history). This is the mean of 35,040 fifteen-minute intervals for the local year, 2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31, using America/Chicago time.

question: Year by year since 2018, what could a four-hour battery have earned per MW in ERCOT with perfect foresight? Which year was highest?
first_answer: This is a model (derived by the ERW), the upper bound a 4-hour battery could have earned with perfect foresight at the hub average. It is not what real batteries earned. Each year is the sum of its monthly rows, in USD per MW (battery_stack_monthly): 2018 243,685; 2019 402,181; 2020 187,481; 2021 3,430,557; 2022 393,104; 2023 530,137; 2024 147,675; 2025 87,440. 2026 is a partial year with 10 months so far: 60,487. The highest year was 2021, at 3,430,557 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly). Winter Storm Uri was in February 2021. The monthly rows are dated by local period, so I used plain calendar years.

question: In the month of 2023 when ERCOT's load paid the most at the hub in real time (load-weighted), what could a four-hour battery have earned per MW with perfect foresight?
answer: The month was August 2023. Its real-time load-weighted hub cost was the highest of 2023 at 220.97 USD/MWh (cost_of_power_monthly, derived by the ERW). In that month a four-hour battery with perfect foresight could have earned about 265,529 USD per MW (265528.8, battery_stack_monthly, derived by the ERW). This is a model upper bound, not what real batteries earned. It is the energy plus ancillary revenue stack at the hub average.

question: What could this battery have earned per MW in July 2025?
answer: In July 2025 (the monthly row dated 2025-07-01), an 8-hour battery using day-ahead prices only could have earned about 7,808 USD per MW (battery_stack_monthly). This is a model result derived by the ERW. It is an upper bound on what a battery could have earned, not what batteries actually earned. No days were left out of the month (0 days, battery_stack_monthly). The figure is per MW and I did not scale it to your 100 MW setting. Settings used: ERCOT hub average, 8 hours, dayahead.
